extracted.intended_audience: citizens/voters considering ratification of the U.S. Constitution; readers of the New York Packet (late-18th-century public)
extracted.subtask_description: A series of late-18th-century political essays (The Federalist) arguing for ratification of the U.S. Constitution, addressing the problems of faction, the advantages of a union, commercial policy, naval power, and revenue policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Causes of faction
rubrics_metrics.description: By a faction, I understand a number of citizens... who are united and actuated by some common impulse of passion, or of interest, adversed to the rights of other citizens, or to the permanent and aggregate interests of the community. The latent causes of faction are thus sown in the nature of man.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies multiple root causes: different opinions (religion, government, speculation/practice), attachment to different leaders, unequal distribution of property, creditors vs. debtors, and other distinct interests (landed, manufacturing, mercantile, moneyed). Use this catalog to analyze why political groupings form and why they are durable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two methods of curing faction
rubrics_metrics.description: There are two methods of curing the mischiefs of faction: the one, by removing its causes; the other, by controlling its effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat as mutually exclusive remedies: attempt to remove causes (e.g., abolish liberty or force uniformity) is unacceptable or impracticable; therefore institutional design should focus primarily on controlling effects. Use this dichotomy when evaluating proposals for addressing factional conflict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liberty must not be sacrificed to cure faction
rubrics_metrics.description: Liberty is to faction what air is to fire, an aliment without which it instantly expires... it would be worse than the disease to destroy the liberty which is essential to its existence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reject any remedy for faction that entails abolishing or unduly restricting political liberty. Institutional criteria should preserve free exercise of reason and liberty even if they enable factions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniformity of opinion is impracticable
rubrics_metrics.description: The second expedient [making every citizen the same in opinion, passion, interest] is as impracticable as the first would be unwise. As long as the reason of man continues fallible... different opinions will be formed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not evaluate constitutional designs on the assumption that opinions can be homogenized. Accept pluralism as intrinsic and design systems that manage diversity rather than eliminate it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control the effects of faction through republican mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: If a faction consists of less than a majority, relief is supplied by the republican principle, which enables the majority to defeat its sinister views by regular vote... To secure the public good and private rights against the danger of such a faction, and at the same time to preserve the spirit and the form of popular government, is the great object.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer institutions (representation, regular voting, checks) that allow peaceful defeat of dangerous minorities and protect rights against majority tyranny. When evaluating a constitution or polity, test whether it balances majority rule with protections for rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pure democracy cannot cure faction
rubrics_metrics.description: A pure democracy... can admit of no cure for the mischiefs of faction. A common passion or interest will, in almost every case, be felt by a majority of the whole... nothing to check the inducements to sacrifice the weaker party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat direct, small-scale democracies as vulnerable to majority oppression and turbulence; favor representative structures to mitigate this vulnerability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation refines and enlarges public views
rubrics_metrics.description: The delegation of the government... to a small number of citizens elected by the rest... is, on the one hand, to refine and enlarge the public views, by passing them through the medium of a chosen body of citizens, whose wisdom may best discern the true interest of their country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate representative bodies on their capacity to 'refine and enlarge' public sentiment — i.e., to filter transient or local passions and deliberate in the national interest. Also note the warning that representatives may be corrupted by intrigue or local prejudice; design safeguards accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Larger republics increase the probability of electing fit representatives
rubrics_metrics.description: If the proportion of fit characters be not less in the large than in the small republic, the former will present a greater option, and consequently a greater probability of a fit choice... chosen by a greater number of citizens... more difficult for unworthy candidates to practice with success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing electoral systems or districting, consider scale: larger electorates per representative make corruption and local cabals harder and broaden the pool of qualified candidates. Beware extremes — too large can disconnect reps from local concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extended sphere (territory/population) checks factious combinations
rubrics_metrics.description: The smaller the society, the fewer probably will be the distinct parties and interests... Extend the sphere, and you take in a greater variety of parties and interests; you make it less probable that a majority of the whole will have a common motive to invade the rights of other citizens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use geographic and demographic scope as a metric for institutional resilience to faction: broader unions aggregate diverse interests and make concerted oppression less likely. Evaluate federations/unions positively in this light.

rubrics_metrics.name: Union (federal structure) is a republican remedy for faction
rubrics_metrics.description: Hence, it clearly appears, that the same advantage which a republic has over a democracy... is enjoyed by a large over a small republic,--is enjoyed by the Union over the States composing it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure the value of a federal union by its capacity to enlarge the representative sphere, diversify interests, and impose obstacles to concert among unjust majorities. Use union as a specific institutional tool to control factional effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unified commercial policy increases international bargaining power
rubrics_metrics.description: By prohibitory regulations, extending, at the same time, throughout the States, we may oblige foreign countries to bid against each other, for the privileges of our markets... we may counteract a policy so unfriendly to our prosperity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess commercial/regulatory regimes by their coordination: a single, nation-wide commercial policy increases leverage in negotiations (e.g., exclusion, tariffs) and can extract concessions; fragmented policy weakens bargaining position.

rubrics_metrics.name: A federal navy enhances national bargaining power and protects commerce
rubrics_metrics.description: The establishment of a federal navy... would put it in our power, at a period not very distant, to create a navy which... would at least be of respectable weight... A few ships of the line, sent opportunely... would often be sufficient to decide the fate of a campaign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating national security and commercial protection, include naval capability and the ability to project limited force as criteria for defending trade, securing neutrality, and obtaining diplomatic concessions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disunion produces passive commerce and vulnerability
rubrics_metrics.description: In a state so insignificant our commerce would be a prey to the wanton intermeddlings of all nations at war with each other... The rights of neutrality will only be respected when they are defended by an adequate power. A nation, despicable by its weakness, forfeits even the privilege of being neutral.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat state weakness and disunity as criteria predicting loss of commercial autonomy, reduced profits (foreign carriers/intermediaries capturing trade margins), and exposure to foreign depredations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certain trade rights are national and require Union (fisheries, lakes, Mississippi)
rubrics_metrics.description: There are rights of great moment to the trade of America which are rights of the Union--I allude to the fisheries, to the navigation of the Western lakes, and to that of the Mississippi. The dissolution of the Confederacy would give room for delicate questions concerning the future existence of these rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assigning jurisdiction or evaluating boundary/sovereignty arrangements, treat fisheries and major waterways as national assets that benefit from unified control and protection; fragmentation risks disadvantageous settlements with foreign powers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pooling regional resources facilitates a national navy
rubrics_metrics.description: A navy of the United States, as it would embrace the resources of all, is an object far less remote than a navy of any single State... different portions of confederated America possess each some peculiar advantage... Southern States furnish naval stores; some yield better iron; seamen chiefly from the Northern hive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess military/defense proposals by whether they leverage complementary regional resources (materials, skilled labor, manpower) across a union and thereby achieve capabilities unattainable by individual parts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commerce as the primary source of national wealth and revenue
rubrics_metrics.description: The prosperity of commerce... has become a primary object of their political cares. By multiplying the means of gratification, by promoting the introduction and circulation of the precious metals... it serves to vivify and invigorate the channels of industry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating economic policy, prioritize measures that foster commerce because they increase money circulation, land value, and the tax base. Use commercial prosperity as a leading indicator of fiscal capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect taxation (imposts/duties) is the practicable revenue base
rubrics_metrics.description: In so opulent a nation as that of Britain... far the greatest part of the national revenue is derived from taxes of the indirect kind, from imposts, and from excises. In America, it is evident that we must a long time depend for the means of revenue chiefly on such duties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor customs duties and other indirect taxes over extensive direct taxation or excises in societies averse to intrusive tax collection; design the revenue system around trade taxes, especially during early stages of commercial development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Union simplifies and secures collection of duties and reduces illicit trade
rubrics_metrics.description: As far as it would contribute to rendering regulations for the collection of the duties more simple and efficacious, so far it must serve to answer the purposes of making the same rate of duties more productive... The facility of communication... would conspire to render an illicit trade between them a matter of little difficulty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate fiscal arrangements for uniformity and enforceability: a centralized/customs union reduces evasion, avoids competitive undercutting of duties among subunits, and increases overall revenue yield.
